reason: The premise that lattice distortions reduce thermal conductivity is supported by E1 and E5, but these refer to different material systems (porous HECs and a generic HEA), not specifically CoCrFeMnNi. The use of DFT for phonon calculations is shown in E2 for SrTiO3, not HEAs. The application of ML for property prediction is mentioned in E3 and E4, but for yield strength and elastic constants, not thermal conductivity. No cited evidence directly supports the specific integration of DFT and ML for thermal conductivity in CoCrFeMnNi, nor the claimed 20% improvement or the applicability limits.
premises: Severe lattice distortions in HEAs reduce phonon group velocities and enhance phonon scattering, leading to low thermal conductivity.
DFT can accurately capture lattice distortions and local bonding heterogeneity in CoCrFeMnNi.
Integrating DFT-derived descriptors into an ML model improves thermal conductivity prediction accuracy over empirical/CALPHAD methods.
The approach is applicable to single-phase CoCrFeMnNi HEAs up to ~600 K.
A 20% improvement in prediction error is achievable with this DFT-ML approach.
